title: Principal singularity pairs and finite unions over characteristic-zero fields
statement: For a scheme $X$ [def-pc-scheme] and a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf $I$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], a principal singularity pair is an affine $X$ with $I=\widetilde{(\pi)}$ for a global section $\pi$ that is a non-zero-divisor in $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and with $X\setminus V(I)$ regular [def-weil-regular-scheme]. It is a characteristic-zero variety pair if there exist a field $K$ of characteristic zero and a finite-type structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. A finite characteristic-zero singularity pair is a pair isomorphic to a finite disjoint union of these pairs: there exist $n\geq0$, schemes $V_i$, ideals $J_i$ and an isomorphism $X\simeq\coprod_{i\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}V_i$ under which the extension of $I$ on each component is $J_i$ and every $(V_i,J_i)$ is a characteristic-zero variety pair. Fields on different components may differ; the empty union is allowed.

source.place: Temkin, Non-embedded Desingularization, proof of Proposition 3.3.5, printed p.25; finite disjoint unions as in §2.1.14
